_notes: Planet surfaces for the game prototype (game/): a hex grid on 3D terrain. The game starts in orbit: the scan shows terrain and rough deposit hints per region; the player picks a landing site, the colony pod descends, and survey rovers reveal exact deposits as they drive. terrain: move_cost = effort to enter a tile (unit speed is effort per second); height = visual relief level. planets: per planet class, how a surface is generated. Elevation and moisture come from deterministic noise (feature_size = tiles per noise cell) and are ranked, so thresholds are shares of the map: elevation ocean 0.30 = the lowest 30% of tiles are ocean, below shallows = shallows, from hills up = hills, from mountains up = mountains, the rest is lowland; within lowland, moisture picks the terrain; polar_rows at top and bottom become polar_terrain. deposits: rolled per tile on matching terrain (coastal = must touch water); amounts are ranges. hints: region totals below likely = traces, below rich = likely, otherwise rich. landing: where a colony pod may set down (tile terrain, and every neighbour must be passable land), how long it falls, what it brings (start_stock, the hub building, units) and how far the landing reveals. build_menu: buildings the player can place on the surface (their costs and stats are in buildings.json: build_seconds, output_per_min, upkeep_per_min, extract_per_min, requires_deposit; the hub's build_radius and build_queues limit where and how many build at once). Tiles must be surveyed and buildable to build on. Power: power_resource (energy) is not stockpiled on a surface; each base (a colony core and the buildings in its radius) has a power budget: power_supply of its working buildings vs power_use; when use exceeds supply, every power user at that base runs at supply/use speed. Levels: a core upgrades along upgrades_to (Colony Hub 1 → Colonial Administration 2 → Planetary Capital 3), paying the next level's cost and taking its build_seconds; it keeps working meanwhile. Storage: stockpiled materials (everything except storage_exempt) share one capacity per player, the sum of storage on their finished buildings (the hub's vault, Storage Containers, refineries); mining stops when it is full. Hills and plains hold raw ore, which an Ore Refinery turns into metal. salvage_refund: share of the cost returned when a finished building is salvaged. units: speed = move effort per second; cost and build_seconds = what a Vehicle Bay charges and takes to assemble one; a unit with extract_per_min is a mining crawler: it unfurls on a deposit (deploy_seconds), fills a hopper and sends each full load home as a cargo pod that flies pod_speed tiles per second to the nearest storage building or refinery. breakdown: while mining, each minute has chance_per_min of a breakdown; the severity is picked by weight and knocks damage (a range) off its integrity (100 = perfect); an explosion also loses the load in the hopper. A broken crawler folds up, can't mine, and drives slower (down to slowest_drive of its speed at 0 integrity). repair: drive it onto a colony core's tile (the repair pad beside the hub); after crew_seconds (the repair crew walking out) it regains per_second integrity, paying cost_per_point for each point, until it is back to 100. hud_resources: the stockpiled resources shown in the top bar, in order. All numbers are placeholders.
